facts.text: The brown thornbill has large dark red eyes and a tawny rump, with blackish streaks on its grey throat and breast.
facts.quote: It has buff scallops on the forehead and large dark red eyes. There are blackish streaks on a grey throat and breast, a tawny rump and tail base

facts.text: Brown thornbills are skilled mimics, copying the alarm calls of other birds such as the New Holland honeyeater to deter predators.
facts.quote: Adult brown thornbills are able to mimic the alarm calls of other birds such as the New Holland honeyeater that warn of a raptor approaching, which deters other predators such as pied currawongs from attacking their nests.

facts.text: Its calls range from a mellow baritone pee-orr to high whistles with rapid cascading trills, described as a rich, musical warble.
facts.quote: The calls have been described as "rich, musical warble". Their calls vary from a mellow baritone pee-orr, high whistles with rapid cascading trills, to many squeaks and churrs.

facts.text: It mainly eats insects, including spiders, beetles, ants and grasshoppers, sometimes supplementing with seeds, fruit or nectar.
facts.quote: The brown thornbill is mainly an insectivore, including spiders, beetles, lerp insects, ants and grasshoppers in its diet. However, it may sometimes eat seeds, fruit, or nectar.

facts.text: Brown thornbills build dome-shaped nests with a hooded side entrance, lightly bound with spider webs and set low among ferns or tussocks.
facts.quote: Their nests are dome-shaped with a hooded side-entrance and built out of grasses, bark shreds, moss and feathers or plant down, lightly bound with spider webs, and usually set low in the undergrowth among ferns or tussocks.

facts.text: The brown thornbill lives in eastern and south-eastern Australia, including Tasmania, usually within 300 kilometres of the coast.
facts.quote: The brown thornbill can be found in the eastern and southeastern parts of Australia, including Tasmania. It is usually found within 300 kilometres (190 mi) of the coast.

facts.text: It is a skilled mimic, and also responds to humans imitating its calls.
facts.quote: Brown thornbills are skilled mimics and also respond to humans imitating their calls.

facts.text: It forages restlessly near the ground and in low trees and shrubs of the understory, often joining groups with other thornbills.
facts.quote: It feeds restlessly close to the ground, in lower trees and shrubs of the understory. It often feeds in groups with other thornbills, except during the breeding season.

facts.text: It forms mixed-species feeding flocks with the yellow-rumped thornbill, the white-browed scrubwren, the speckled warbler and the eastern yellow robin.
facts.quote: It also forms mixed-species feeding flocks with the yellow-rumped thornbill (Acanthiza chrysorrhoa), the white-browed scrubwren (Sericornis frontalis), the speckled warbler (Pyrrholaemus sagittatus), and the eastern yellow robin (Eopsaltria australis).

facts.text: Brown thornbill pairs tend to stay together for a long time.
facts.quote: Brown thornbill couples tend to pair for a long time.
